transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been troubling you or what brings you in today?

Um, yeah… I guess it’s not an emergency or anything, but I’ve noticed I’m kind of arranging my day around avoiding elevators. Like, I’ll take five flights of stairs at home instead, and I turned down a workshop because it was in a high-rise. I’ve also stopped visiting one of my older computer students because his building doesn’t really have another option. It feels a little silly saying it out loud, but it’s starting to get in the way.
Can you tell me what goes through your mind or how you feel when you think about using an elevator?

I mean… logically I know elevators in an office building are probably safe. It’s not like I really think every one is going to fail. But when I’m standing there looking at the doors—especially the older ones in my apartment building or at work—my brain kind of treats it like I’m about to get stuck inside, or like it could drop. I know that sounds a bit dramatic, but that’s where my mind goes.
Does this kind of anxious reaction happen in other situations, or is it mostly limited to when you’re thinking about using an elevator?

It’s mostly elevators, I think. I mean, I know an elevator in an office building is probably safe, and I don’t want to make it sound bigger than it is. But when I’m looking at those older doors in my apartment building or at work, my mind just kind of jumps to being trapped in there or it dropping, even though part of me knows that’s probably over the top.
Are there other situations or places where you feel similar anxiety or avoid going, or is it mainly limited to elevators?

It’s mainly elevators, I think. I don’t really have that same feeling in most other places. It’s just… when I see the older elevator doors at my apartment or at work, even though I know it’s probably safe, my mind goes straight to, “What if I get trapped in there?” or “What if it drops?” I know that probably sounds over the top, but that’s the thing that sets it off.

When you're faced with the idea of getting into an elevator or standing near the doors, do you ever feel a sudden rush of intense anxiety or physical symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, or shortness of breath?

Yeah… I mean, not every single time, but pretty quickly, yeah. If I step toward an elevator or even hear it sort of clunk open, my chest tightens and my hands get sweaty. It’s like this quick rush of panic before I’ve really even thought about it. I know that probably sounds a little much, but that’s what happens.
